title: Split a virtual address
description:
Write `split(address)`, which splits a 64-bit x64 virtual address into the parts the MMU uses:

- `offset`: the low 12 bits;
- `level1` to `level4`: four 9-bit table indices, `level1` from bits 12 to 20, `level2` from bits 21 to 29, `level3` from bits 30 to 38, `level4` from bits 39 to 47;
- `canonical`: true if bits 48 to 63 are all equal to bit 47.

Also write `pageNumber(address)`, the address shifted right by 12.

```
split(0x00007FF6A1234567):
  offset 0x567, level1 0x34, level2 0x109, level3 0x1DA, level4 0xFF, canonical
```
hints: Each field is "shift down to bit 0, then mask": `(address >> 21) & 0x1FF` keeps the 9 bits starting at bit 21.
For the canonical check, look at bits 47 to 63 together (`address >> 47`, 17 bits): they must be all zeros or all ones (`0x1FFFF`).
